title: Your Business Phone System Costs Way More Than You Think (Here's Why)
excerpt: You're probably leaving money on the table with hidden fees — and there's a smarter way to buy.

content.text: So I was digging through what people are actually paying for business phone systems right now, and honestly? It's a mess. You see $15 a month advertised, and then suddenly you're getting invoiced $50+ per person. The gap between what companies think they're paying and what they're actually paying is genuinely wild.

Here's the thing: most business phone systems quote you a base price per user per month — that's the headline number. But that's never the full story. You've got setup fees, installation costs, feature add-ons (call recording, call forwarding, voicemail transcription), taxes, and integration fees if you want it to talk to your CRM or accounting software. By the time you're actually using the thing, the real cost per person can be double or triple what you saw in that first quote.
The range right now is $15–$50+ per user per month — but most small businesses end up somewhere in the $35–$45 range once everything's added up.
Why This Matters to You Specifically

items: You're paying more than you budgeted, and that adds up fast across even a small team
Hidden fees often mean you're locked into long contracts before you realize what you're actually spending
You might be paying for features you'll never use because they're bundled in, not optional
The "cheap" option ends up being more expensive than the mid-tier choice once you add what you actually need

content.label: Intecha's Take
content.text: Don't just look at the per-user price — ask for the all-in monthly cost for your exact team size, with every fee spelled out. Get it in writing. Then ask what happens if you add two people, or if you want call recording, or if you need to integrate it with your other tools. Make them show you the real number before you sign anything. And honestly? Compare at least three options side-by-side using the same requirements. You'll spot the honest players pretty quick — they'll give you that breakdown without hedging.

One more thing: if you're currently with a system and haven't looked at your bill in a while, pull it up today. Seriously. I've talked to so many small business owners who didn't realize they were paying for features they removed two years ago, or they were on an old tier that costs more than the current equivalent. A quick audit takes 20 minutes and could save you hundreds a month.
